← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Pan source-view and camera audit — 2026-10-14

The official GM photos support a shallow extension beside the deeper sump. The earlier proxy instead had a full-depth solid block beneath its raised interior shelf. This revision removes that exterior block. It retains the 474.7 × 316 × 117.99 mm published maximum envelope, all outline vertices, the cavity-facing shelf, vertical transition wall and floor, and the cover/pickup/insert placements.

This is a topology correction to an illustrative context. Neither the outline nor the shelf transition is a calibrated reconstruction. The new underside Z=70 mm and remaining 4 mm shelf skin are explicit, unmeasured proxy choices; they are not dimensions extracted from a photograph.

The retained official photos are separately identified in oil-pan-evidence/artifact-manifest.json. Pixel regions below are approximate visual locators in the original images, measured from the top-left; they are not fitted landmarks or dimensional measurements.

The long model axis is Y, positive toward the cover/tube region; X spans width and Z rises from the deepest assumed exterior floor. No mapping to installed vehicle forward/left is recovered.

Additional reseller viewpoints

Three additional GMPartsGiant 12601240 gallery images were retrieved and retained with URLs, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes in pan-camera-audit/manifest.json. They show opposing assembled-pan views, including the broad shallow extension and the shorter region beyond the deep exterior basin. All three retain the silver baffle and pickup relief. A preliminary description of the first as an uncovered cavity was rejected after direct inspection; no baffle-off view was recovered. The additional angles corroborate shallow-versus-deep exterior topology but do not establish casting thickness, hidden floor or transition coordinates. These are reseller images associated with the exact-part listing, with less direct provenance than the official GM assets.

Camera and scale audit

The independent model views are top, side, and underside. They use the saved baseline exploded STEP, with the pan shell focused; other components appear faintly as context. Its existing cutaway removes part of the +X wall. The top and underside views must therefore not be read as complete casting silhouettes. The side view exposes the shallow-end relief; the underside reveals its boundary across the shelf footprint. The ordinary cutaway and section show its relationship to the unchanged cavity and insert.

The model cameras are orthographic (top, right, and direction −1/−1/−1). The photographs have unknown focal length, pose, perspective and crop. No camera solve, image rectification or metric pixel scale is claimed. The official maximum envelope includes protruding casting features; assigning that full width to a selected inner edge would produce a false scale. Even the plane of the shelf differs from the flange plane. A whole-image pixel ratio cannot resolve shelf height, boss coordinates or hidden floor geometry.

Before-edit views and their STEP/photo hashes were retained in local history. Current snapshot outputs are bound to the saved STEP and camera commands by the normal render receipt. The before-edit side/underside views showed a flat bottom across the full pan length; this contradicted the visible shallow exterior extension irrespective of camera calibration.

Adopted change and retained values

Parameter or featureDecisionEvidence limit
Published maximum envelopeRetain 474.7 × 316 × 117.99 mmSource-backed maximum only; does not validate the polygon.
PAN_OUTLINE_XY and inner scalesRetain all valuesPhotos show a more complex casting, but no calibrated boundary or wall offset. Do not move vertices by eye and call them recovered coordinates.
Shelf plan regionRetain center (0, −150), size 400 × 220, clipped to the pan outline; positive-Y boundary −40 mmExisting unmeasured proxy. Cover occlusion prevents locating the real transition.
Shelf topRetain Z=74 mm, from floor Z=4 plus shelf height 70Existing unmeasured proxy; not narrowed by the photos.
PAN_SHELF_UNDERSIDE_ZAdopt Z=70 mm; remove material below it within the shelf footprint, stopping 4 mm short of the deep-side edge to retain the transition wallShallow exterior topology is visible; this numeric depth is a design assumption. The 4 mm residual skin reuses the existing nominal floor thickness as a display choice, not an OEM thickness.
Shelf transition, ribs, flanges and earsKeep simplified sharp transition and existing interior rib cuesActual radii, draft, local steps, second shallow-end region, ribs, bosses and mounting ears remain unresolved. This change does not claim full exterior likeness.
Deep floor, pickup, tube, cover and mountsRetain existing proxies and missing-mount designationHidden interfaces remain unmeasured; no new fit clearance or attachment coordinates adopted.

The shared parameter source and generated dimension register identify the new underside as DISPLAY_PROXY_ASSUMPTION. The construction rejects an underside below zero or at/above the shelf top. A small geometry regression compares revised and legacy shells in each of the five contexts: one valid connected solid, unchanged envelope, only material removal within the declared underside region, a continuous retained shelf skin, and the full legacy vertical transition wall. It tests the whole shell without the presentation cutaway.

The existing saved-solid fit, gate, assembly-route and tooling checks remain the basis for A/B/C comparison. This correction does not rank oil-control performance, establish a new service route, or turn scenario ranges into confidence intervals. The first relief attempt left an opening through the vertical shelf transition. Visual review rejected it; the repaired cut retains a 4 mm wall on the shelf side of that boundary, and a regression compares that full wall against the legacy solid. The wall thickness is also an unmeasured display assumption. The corrected saved-solid report preserves all fit, motion, removal-path, sensitivity, gravity and accessory-study results. All 312 cylindrical-tool approach statuses and obstacle lists are also unchanged. Only 24 installed approaches have smaller overlap volumes with the thinner shelf-transition wall; all remain blocked. Final release requires the full media/check pipeline and independent frozen-candidate review.

Next discriminating digital evidence

Additional exact-part photographs from a different side may refine the exterior transition and opposite shallow-end topology. A view with the cover removed could expose cavity topology. A recoverable calibrated multi-view set or dimensioned source would be needed before narrowing the interior coordinates. Until then, retain independent proxy scenarios rather than inventing correlated fit bounds. No physical measurement is a prerequisite to this digital work.
